summary: Shape classes for bacteria exist at scale (Madin et al. trait synthesis, ~170k strain records; BacDive, 100k strains behind a free token), but their vocabulary is rod/coccus/spiral and cannot distinguish an unduloid from a cylinder. For protists and algae only image collections exist (Cell Image Library, EcoTaxa, BioImage Archive studies), none annotated by Plateau surface family, and time-lapse of growth transitions is available only per model-organism study. A test needs outlines to be fitted, not looked up.
next_step: Define the surface-family classifier and apply it to outlines from a stratified sample: EcoTaxa protist objects, CIL unicellular images and a bacterial time-lapse study from BioImage Archive; report frequencies by family and transitions during division.
obstacles_confirmed: Bacterial vocabularies collapse unduloids into rods or spirals.
Protist coverage in open shape tables is much thinner than bacterial coverage.
Transitions during growth need time series, which these archives mostly lack.
